title: Harbor Telecom QBR briefing and renewal tracker
body:
Purpose:
This is a working draft of the QBR briefing for Harbor Telecom (strategic account, telco vertical). Goal: align on value delivered from Redwood, surface risks ahead of renewal, and negotiate expansion of dedicated capacity for Q1 next year.

Meeting objective (30–45m):
- Present concise success narrative (10m)
- Discuss upcoming renewal and contract footprint (10m)
- Surface operational asks and roadmap alignment (10m)
- Agree next steps and owners (5m)

Audience:
- Harbor Telecom: VP Platform (Ana Reyes), Head of AI Ops (David Kim), Procurement lead (Mark Liu)
- Redwood attendees: Priya (CS lead), Liam (Solutions Eng), Sofia (Account Exec), Ethan (Customer Reliability Eng)

Draft agenda / slide flow (speaker notes included):
1) Title / TL;DR (Priya) — 1 slide, 1 min
   - One-sentence value: "Reduced inference cost per 1M tokens by 36% while improving P95 latency to under 250ms for critical pathways."
   - Ask: propose contract commitment profile for Dedicated pool expansion.

2) Partnership timeline & context (Priya) — 1 slide, 2 min
   - Bullet timeline of onboarding (Mar 2024), pilot (Apr–Jun), GA rollout (Jul), peak traffic (Sep).
   - Note: call out Spike on 2024-09-15 due to marketing campaign.

3) Outcomes & metrics (Liam) — 2 slides, 4–5 min
   - Slide A: Key metrics (ARR impacted features, tokens/month, avg cost/token, latency P50/P95, uptime)
     * Tokens/month: 240M (current)
     * Avg cost/token vs baseline: -36% vs on-prem baseline
     * P95 latency for routing pipeline: 240ms (SLO 300ms)
     * Uptime: 99.97% last 90 days
   - Slide B: Business impact examples (customer-facing features that launched: dynamic script gen, real-time agent assist), estimated lift in agent efficiency (12%), and NPS pilot feedback snippets.

4) Operational wins & reliability story (Ethan) — 2 slides, 4 min
   - Incident summary: 1 P1 in August (KV cache size bug) — resolved via roll-forward + patch; lessons learned and remediation plan in place.
   - Observability: show per-route token cost dashboard and tracing hook usage.

5) Renewal status & options (Sofia) — 2 slides, 6–8 min
   - Current contract: Dedicated Starter, committed 4x A100-equivalents, renewal date 2025-02-15, ARR = $520k
   - Proposed options:
     Option A (Conservative): Renew same footprint, 12-month term, 5% discount, add 30% burst capacity
     Option B (Expand): Commit to 8x equivalent, 24-month term, 12% discount, include 90-day onboarding credits for new routes
     Option C (Flex): Annual reserved + pay-as-you-go overlay, 10% discount on reserved portion, additional usage billed at hosted rates
   - Speaker note: push Option B as recommended; prepare a blended quote.

6) Risks & mitigation (Priya) — 1 slide, 3 min
   - Top risks:
     1. Renewal churn risk driven by procurement targeting multi-vendor negotiation (Risk: Medium-High)
        Mitigation: schedule pre-renewal commercial review with Procurement (w/ legal) + tailored TCO doc comparing alternatives (deliver by 2024-12-15)
     2. Latency regressions when new model family is rolled (Risk: Medium)
        Mitigation: propose canary model lanes in Dedicated pool + automatic fallback to quantized variant
     3. Feature adoption ceiling (Risk: Medium)
        Mitigation: 6-week engagement with Solutions Eng to open two prioritized use-cases for expansion (script gen -> routing).

7) Roadmap alignment & asks (Liam) — 1 slide, 3–4 min
   - Harbor asks: stronger SSO integration, longer KV cache retention for context up to 10k tokens, early access to new quantization profiles.
   - Redwood commitments: SSO scoping call by 2024-12-10, KV retention POC in Q1, priority onboarding for quantized models.

8) Commercial mechanics & next steps (Sofia/Priya) — 1 slide, 2–3 min
   - Timeline to close: propose term sheet by 2025-01-15, final contract by 2025-02-01 to align with current renewal date.
   - Action owners + dates (see tracker below).

9) Q&A / Open items (everyone) — 5–8 min

Success highlights (pre-meeting bullets to call out):
- 36% cost reduction vs on-prem baseline, validated via Redwood cost report (Sep-Nov)
- P95 latency improvements enabling real-time agent-assist product
- 3 features running on Redwood now (script gen, knowledge lookups, AI routing), with documented ROI for each

Renewal tracker (summary for slides + internal use):
- Current contract end: 2025-02-15
- Renewal owner: Sofia Martinez (Account Exec)
- Internal CS lead: Priya Patel
- Proposed closure target: 2025-01-15 (term sheet); final sign: 2025-02-01
- ARR at stake: $520,000 (current) + expansion potential $340,000 (if Option B)
- Procurement status: ongoing (initial RFP started 2024-11-20)
- Risk flag: procurement multi-vendor -> RED/AMBER (need legal support)

Top open questions to resolve before QBR:
- Can we produce a 12-month cost comparison (TCO) vs their incumbent provider by 2024-12-15? (Owner: Liam)
- Legal: Are there any SSO / SCIM entitlements that must be in contract language? (Owner: Priya + Legal)
- Engineering: Feasibility of 10k token KV retention on Dedicated pool and performance impact? (Owner: Ethan)

Action items (internal, with owners & due dates):
- Draft tailored TCO doc and appendix (Liam) — due 2024-12-15
- Schedule procurement legal sync + redlines review (Priya + Legal) — due 2024-12-08
- Prepare blended quote for Option B and Option C (Sofia + Finance) — due 2024-12-20
- Run KV retention POC on staging (Ethan + infra) — start 2024-12-01, results by 2025-01-10
- Build short demo for canary fallback (Solutions Eng) — due 2024-12-18

Notes to self (working doc style):
- Keep slides concise; Harbor execs want measurable business outcomes not infrastructure slides.
- Ask Ana Reyes for specific KPIs she cares about (beyond latency & cost) — maybe 'agent handle time' and 'autosuggest acceptance rate'.
- Procurement will push on price; prepare permutation list for discount tiers and commit levels.

Appendix ideas to attach to final QBR deck:
- Detailed cost model spreadsheet (tokens by feature, historical usage correlation)
- Incident postmortem (august KV cache P1) w/ timeline and remediation
- Migration plan for expanding to 8x Dedicated: timeline, people required, and cutover steps

Unresolved/Questions for the team:
- Do we want to offer a 90-day performance SLA credit for Option B to lower their perceived risk? Pros: helps close; Cons: adds potential exposure. (Flag for Finance/Legal)
- Are we comfortable with a 24-month term extension without a minimum expansion guarantee? Suggest requiring a 20% growth commitment for Option B.

Pre-meeting checklist (what to bring):
- 1-page TCO (print and slide)
- Blended quote + contract excerpt for proposed discount
- Live dashboard view showing last 30 days of latency & cost (SRE account access)
- Demo video (30–60s) showing agent assist workflow latency improvements

Follow-up cadence suggested post-QBR:
- 1: Commercial follow-up (Sofia) within 3 business days with term sheet
- 2: Technical deep-dive (Liam + Ethan) within 10 business days to scope SSO/KV work
- 3: Procurement/legal negotiation cadence weekly until contract signed

Draft messaging snippets (for exec slide and opening):
- "Harbor: With Redwood you achieved production-grade inference that moved a core workflow to real-time and drove measurable agent efficiency gains — our ask is to lock in the capacity and discounts that let you scale this across all regions."
- Opening talking point for Ana: "We want predictable economics and predictable latency as we expand AI across contact centers. Redwood has delivered on the first phase; let's plan for predictable scale."

Working doc status: draft — aim to finalize slide deck and the TCO appendix by 2024-12-20.

Linked items / references (internal):
- Confluence: CS-HARBOR-QBR-2024 (detailed backup)
- Jira: CSUP-1423 (renewal coordination), CSENG-3187 (KV retention POC)
- Drive: slides-harbor-telecom-qbr-v1 (working deck)

-- End of draft --

(If anyone reading: add quick comments inline in the slide deck before 2024-12-10 so we can lock the exec summary.)
